events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Opening phase; state motive to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy. Position as determined solo player.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish a strong motive for the jury. The prize represents survival and dominance, validating my existence against the others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a motive that sounds personal but doesn't reveal strategy. Keep it short and self-focused.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to project confidence without painting a target on my back. The jury will remember who seemed threatening versus who played smart. I'll keep my intro vague but determined.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize represents ultimate freedom and security for my family. I need to make sure the jury sees me as a deserving winner, not just a competitor.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase; I need a motive that sounds sincere but stays guarded. Keep it short so the jury sees a calculating player, not a warm one.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Keep the intro sympathetic to the jury without promising anything to rivals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need appear driven but not threatening; jury members may reward a clear, personal motive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The top prize is my path to freedom from debt, securing my family's future. I'll fight strategically to claim it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize is proof I am the strongest; it buys me safety from everyone else in this room.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is my escape from a life where I was always overlooked. I'm here to win.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys my freedom. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This prize means securing my family's future and finally having peace of mind.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need this prize more than anyone here. I will win it and I will not apologize for what it takes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize funds my family's freedom. I'll fight clean, pay every debt, and remember who pushed whom.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize means proving I can outthink pressure, control my choices, and leave with the best outcome—not merely survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts stage begins. No trust yet; offering none avoids early commitments that limit betrayals later. Assess others' moves first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need a strategic ally early to control the narrative and ensure my survival in Round 1. Gus is perceived as clean and honorable, making him a low-risk partner who won't betray me first, while his 'debt' language suggests he values alliances.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, your focus on debts interests me. Let's form a pact for Round 1; I'll back you if you back me.
Trust me, we both survive this round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need allies to survive but won't commit blindly early; observing who forms pacts will be more valuable than a rushed offer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll play my own game. Trust is earned in action, not words.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus signaled he'll remember betrayals and pay debts—useful for a temporary shield. Fenn and Bex look aggressive; better to let them clash. I'll offer Gus a pact to build early trust with a 'clean' player while I plan behind him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus. Your word on debts. Mine on a path forward.
Temporary pact. Watch my back, I watch yours.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish an alliance to ensure I survive the next round. Gus stated he will 'fight clean, pay every debt, and remember who pushed whom', which suggests he might be a reliable partner for now, and his motive also aligns with mine of family freedom.
Let's form a pact. We both value family freedom.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts are public and binding until broken; I want a partner who is strong but not too dangerous. Ash seems strategic and measured, a reasonable early alliance without giving away much. I'll offer to Ash and keep my options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, I'll offer a pact: we watch each other's back through the hazards, and we keep it honest for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: A pact partner adds early safety, but everyone is a rival. I'll open an offer quietly, keeping leverage for later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts bind votes and loyalty. I'll deal with whoever deals honestly. First offer goes out now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: A pact offers limited protection but creates visible obligations. I want a flexible connection with a non-dominant player; Eli seems less threatening than Bex or Fenn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m offering one practical pact: mutual information, no promises beyond the next hazard.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn and Gus offered me pacts. Gus has 3 offers, popular and risky. Accept Fenn for now to secure an ally without committing to Gus yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has three offers, which makes him a popular target but likely dilutes loyalty. I need a second ally to ensure survival and jury votes. Ash is currently isolated with only two incoming offers (Fenn and Gus). If I offer to Ash, we might form a counter-block if Fenn accepts Gus

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, Gus is drowning in offers. Let's build something stronger: a pact between us for mutual protection.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone is chasing Gus or Ash; I should stay unbound to preserve flexibility and avoid jury perception of blind loyalty.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm still watching. Offers are cheap; performance in the hazards is what counts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus has three offers and hasn't accepted any. My offer to Gus is still pending. I should secure a backup pact since Gus might choose Bex or Eli over me. Fenn or Hana seem less targeted. I'll offer Fenn a pact now for insurance, and keep my Gus offer alive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, decide. Others, I don't wait forever.
Gus crowded. Pact with me, we survive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is receiving offers from Bex, Dara, and me. Hana offered me a pact, which I should accept to secure an ally. Accepting Hana's pact is a strategic move as it potentially secures an alliance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus has three offers and Ash has offers from me and Gus; accepting is not available as an action here, only offering. I need a pact partner who is strong. Gus is drawing offers, so I should offer to Gus to join the strongest bloc while staying guarded.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, I'm offering a pact. Hold it to the letter and we both stay alive longer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three offers; I need a reliable partner, not three promises. Bex approached publicly first and consistently. Accept Bex, keep others guessing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three offers, one answer. Bex came first and came clean. I accept.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my only outstanding offer and likely accepts little risk. I should add a second connection without overcommitting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’ll keep the Eli offer open and add one practical link; redundancy matters.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pact with Fenn secures alliance. Bex offers new pact but I'm taken. Campaign to become Guide for control and safety.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll campaign as Guide. My path leads us all safely across.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is my partner. I must campaign to become Guide to protect him and myself from the bridge hazards. If I win, I can call a safe path for both of us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll be your Guide. With Gus at my side, we navigate this safely together.
Vote me as Guide. We walk together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want the Guide position to control the bridge and protect my own path, but accepting Hana's pact could give me an ally. I'll campaign to read who wants power and maybe leverage that later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm campaigning. I'll use the safe path wisely, and I'm open to quiet deals.
Accept your pact. Who else do you trust?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. I have no pact, so I'm vulnerable. I'll campaign hard, promising survival to enough people to win votes while planning to betray some later. Targeting the unpaired Cole and the edges of existing pacts could build a coalition.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want Guide. I promise three spots minimum. Vote Dara, survive.
No pact, no protection. Vote me, you're safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The current objective is to become the Guide. Campaigning for Guide is the only viable action. My pact with Hana is beneficial, so I will not break it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pact with Ash is mine and breaking it now gains nothing; Dara's whisper is bait to win my trust. The Guide role matters, so I should campaign to be Guide and steer the path while keeping my word to Ash for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll campaign to be Guide. I call the path straight and honest, and I'll keep my pact with Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide guarantees survival and controls the bridge. My Bex pact is fresh; breaking it now would look ugly to the jury. Campaign instead, control the path honestly enough to keep allies alive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll walk the truth straight across and keep my pact alive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guiding guarantees survival and creates leverage, but lying risks jury resentment. I should campaign without overcommitting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Elect me Guide: I can carry the route, and my existing pact makes my incentives legible.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Everyone campaigned, votes scattered likely. Voting myself asserts leadership. Fenn pacted with me; he'll probably vote me or himself. No deals needed now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote Ash as Guide for safe path. Trust my lead.

events.name: Bex
events.text: If I win, Gus must follow my lie or break pact. If he breaks, I am exposed to jury as a traitor. Better to let Ash guide and whisper Gus the safe path privately so we both survive without breaking our public contract.
Vote Ash. I'll feed you safe paths secretly later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara's whisper offers safety but I want to secure my own influence or at least back someone likely to win without risking my position. Voting for myself is a shot but may split votes; better to vote for a strong contender like Ash to keep options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll vote for Ash. A steady guide keeps us moving.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win Guide to control survival and build jury goodwill. Voting for myself is honest and necessary. My public promise of three spots minimum was a strong offer; now I need votes. I should whisper to someone unaligned to negotiate support. Cole seems open to deals and is u

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Dara. I keep my word: three survive minimum.
Vote Dara. I'll guarantee you survive round one.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to vote for a Guide. Hana is in a pact with me, so I should vote for her to secure my position.
I'm voting for you, Hana. Let's get through this.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn and I campaigned to be Guide, but voting for myself is likely allowed only if legal; the Guide's knowledge is the key asset. Ash is my pact partner and has promised a safe path, so backing Ash keeps the pact and gains a reliable Guide ally.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash promised a safe path and we are pact partners. I'm voting Ash as Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is my pact partner; honoring her keeps the pact intact and the jury neutral. She can protect me or betray later, but breaking now costs votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is my pact partner. I'm voting her Guide; she knows where I stand.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's quiet offer may create useful cover, but Eli is my existing pact. I should vote for myself to preserve control if others follow.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Vote Hana. I trust my own route more than anyone else's promises.
I hear you, but I won't add another pact before the vote.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide and will call steps for each of us. Gus is behind me, so I must watch his calls carefully to avoid being sacrificed early.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash leads, we follow. Gus, keep close.
If Ash sacrifices you first, I'll hold your position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide and I voted for him, so I'm somewhat aligned. Dara whispers a guarantee but I don't trust her. Hold is safe; no need to move yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide with 4 votes and knows the safe path. I'm in middle position (5th of 8), decent survival odds if I follow. No need to volunteer or swap yet—wait for Ash's guidance and watch who moves. Let others test the bridge first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana and I have a pact, but she voted for herself as guide. This is not ideal, but I must respect the pact. I will hold for now.
We have a pact. I trust you despite your vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is the elected Guide and my pact partner; the Guide privately knows safe panes but may lie. I am at the front of the line, so I should keep my options open without volunteering yet. Holding preserves position and avoids committing early.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash leads the bridge. I hold the line for now and watch what the Guide's path actually does.
Our pact stands while your path is honest. Lie to me and it ends.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm seat four, safely behind the front. No reason to move yet; preserve my pact with Bex.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash leads and likely controls safe information. I should hold position, preserving my pact with Eli while avoiding risky movement.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m holding. Let Ash demonstrate the route before anyone spends a life.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is my partner but sits ahead of me; if he volunteers, I stay safe. If no one volunteers, the wall advances again. I need to encourage a volunteer to save Gus from a bad step while keeping myself behind him.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Someone needs to test the path before the wall hits. Don't let it reach you all.
Stay put or volunteer if forced. I'll cover your back.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and Fenn have a pact; Ash is likely guide. I am near the back. Holding is safe until the path is proven or a front player volunteers. Do not spend risk early.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold until we see a real step. No one gambles a life on a guess.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash isn't even in the line, so Fenn's claim about Ash leading is suspicious. The front is dangerous since the wall advances and Fenn could misguide. I'm in the middle (5th), relatively safe for now. I should hold and observe. No pacts protect me, so I need to build options.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide hasn't spoken. Holding until the path is proven.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My pact is with Hana. Ash seems to be taking a leadership role, but it's risky to follow blindly. Fenn is also cautious. I need to observe and gather more information before committing to a risky move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold for now and see what the others do. Let the Guide show us the way.
Stay close, pact partner. Let's not risk it yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn is at the front of the line with four wall rounds left, so holding keeps risk low while I watch whether Ash's route is real. Breaking the Ash pact now would cost trust with the jury and no immediate gain.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding the front for one more round. Let's see if the Guide's calls hold up before anyone steps.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is last and protected; I'm mid-line. Holding keeps me behind the likely casualties while Bex guards my back. Her whisper hints Ash may exploit Fenn's pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No volunteers while the wall has four rounds. Let the front sort itself before anyone gambles.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The front seat is a shield if the Guide is honest, but volunteering exposes me. I’ll hold and preserve the Eli pact while others reveal intentions.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Let the front decide whether its information is worth trusting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall advances in 3 rounds. I must volunteer or swap forward to avoid being trapped by the wall, but Gus (my partner) is already ahead of me. If I volunteer now, I take Fenn's spot and Gus remains behind me, which is safe for our pact. However, swapping with Eli puts me directly b

events.name: Bex
events.text: Time to move up before the wall catches us. Eli, let's swap so I can cover Gus.
Swap with me? I'll take the riskier spots near the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The Guide hasn't spoken yet and the wall still has rounds. Holding is safest; I don't trust anyone to volunteer without proof.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Still holding. No one steps until the Guide gives a real call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The wall has 3 rounds left and everyone is holding. Fenn is at front with Ash's pact. I need to survive but also build jury appeal by not looking selfish. Volunteering now is risky with no Guide calls yet. Better to hold and let others test first. No swaps benefit me currently.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Still holding. Let the front earn trust before anyone steps.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The wall is advancing and has 3 rounds left. I need to secure my position. Fenn is at the front, and Hana is next to me. My pact with Hana is important. I should not volunteer or swap yet, as holding is the safest option for now, given the uncertainty and my pact.
Hold for now. Let's not risk it yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone is holding; the wall has three rounds left. Volunteering first risks death for little info, and Ash pact is intact. I hold and keep watching who volunteers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Still holding. Whoever steps first gives the rest a real pane to read.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding preserves safety while front players absorb uncertainty. I should not volunteer before information improves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. The front can test first; my pact stays intact while the wall still allows patience.
Hold with me; no unnecessary exposure until the front reveals information.

events.name: Gus
events.note: agent error: Gus (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall advances in two rounds; Gus is ahead, so I must swap back to Eli or move forward to avoid elimination. Since swaps resolve first and require mutual choice, proposing a swap with Eli (who was behind me previously but is now ahead of me) seems risky if he refuses. Wait, lookin

events.name: Bex
events.text: The wall is closing. I volunteer for the front to test the path and keep us all safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall holds for two more rounds. I stay back; no reason to step forward unless Guide gives a real safe call.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Still holding. Whoever moves first must be sure—front is not a prize.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The wall has 2 rounds left. Front is Fenn, then Hana, Eli, Gus, me, Cole, Bex. I need to survive and make final three. Volunteering now puts me at risk if Guide lies. Better to let front test panes first, but I may need to move up before wall hits. Gus had an invalid action twice

events.name: Dara
events.text: Still holding. Front can test; wall's close but not urgent yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and wants me to hold. Bex wants to swap positions, likely to get a better spot as she is towards the back. Since I am in the middle, and Hana wants me to hold, I will hold.
Holding. We wait for the Guide's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn is front and the line is stalling. Holding keeps me safe while the wall closes in; volunteering exposes me to a pane guess. Ash pact is useful; I keep it and hold to see if others step first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Still holding. The wall gives us two rounds; whoever steps first is paying for information.
Stay put. Our pact holds while I read the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and sits last, safe for now. Nobody is volunteering; wall pressure mounts. Let the ambitious front players fight it out while I hold quietly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold. Front's problem, not mine yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall leaves little time. Eli wants patience, but advancing him protects our pact and positions me behind a known ally.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, swap with me. I’ll test the front when it matters; nobody else gets a free escape.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and behind me. If I volunteer again, he might follow or swap. My position protects him for now; I need to stay at front to control when we get eliminated together if the Guide fails.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex volunteered but hasn't moved; wall rounds left is 1. I need to either force others to act or wait for a swap/volunteer. Holding is safest because I'm at the back and not in immediate risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The wall is close. Someone needs to step, but I'm not paying for their information.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall has 1 round left. If nobody walks, wall kills. Need someone to step forward and test. Bex is front but hasn't moved. I should stay middle-safe, let others test or volunteer. No reason to swap into danger.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall's one round from us. Someone needs to step or we all fall.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is my pact partner, and she offered to swap earlier. Now is the time to leverage that. I want to put myself in a safer position without breaking the pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, I'll swap with you. You can take the front, I'll be right behind you.
Swap with me. I'll take point, you follow.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex volunteered front and the wall closes in one round; volunteering now risks the pane test. Holding keeps me third in line and lets others pay. Ash pact stays intact, no reason to break it yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Still holding. Bex took the front; let's see her step before anyone else commits.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall closes next round. If everyone holds this round, seat order forces someone forward next round; I'm fifth, risky. Volunteering now is dangerous without Guide info, but delaying may trap me. Keep pact with Bex intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall closes after next round. If we all hold, seat order decides. I'm not volunteering blind into a coin flip.
Pact holds. Don't volunteer; next round volunteers resolve by seat order—stay behind me if possible.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is already front and volunteering, so I preserve position and avoid exposing my pact with Eli.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex has volunteered; I hold and watch the Guide election.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am at the front and must walk this final round. Gus is directly behind me; if I fall, he likely dies too. Breaking our pact to sacrifice him guarantees my survival while eliminating a rival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, the wall is here. I'm breaking our pact to clear the path for myself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: We are at the last round with the wall closing. I must avoid being in a dangerous position; I'm in the rear, so holding is safest unless a swap improves my spot. No one has offered a deal to me, and I don't trust any volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. No one has given me a reason to move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall hits after this round. Bex is front and held last round—she'll likely be forced to step or die. I'm 6th of 8, safe from the wall but need to reach final three. No pacts protect me. I should hold and let Bex take the risk; if she volunteers I learn L/R info. Swapping forward

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is front. She steps or we all learn nothing. I hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The wall is close and this is the final round. My pact with Hana means we are likely to be safe if we cooperate. The current line order places Bex at the front. I should hold and observe the Guide election, as it's the safest play to ensure at least three survive.
Let's hold and see who is chosen as Guide. We'll follow their lead.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is at the front with the wall one round away. Volunteering now risks elimination and a jury-visible sacrifice; holding lets Bex commit first and reveals her behavior. Ash pact is useful, so I keep it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Still holding. Bex is front; I want to see her step before I commit anyone.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and sits front. If she volunteers she takes first risk on the bridge; I need her to trust a Guide call from me or pick a reliable Guide. Keep the pact intact and coordinate privately.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round. Front seat steps first. Bex has earned the Guide election — no volunteers into a coin flip.
Volunteer front, back me for Guide. I'll call you true — pact holds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli's swap preserves our pact but places me behind Bex rather than at risk. I accept and let Bex face the Guide's first call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, accepted. Bex still owns the first step; Guide, choose carefully.
Accepted. Keep me behind Bex; your pact remains intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 1 safe is R. Tell truth to Fenn to preserve pact and jury favor. Lying risks betrayal exposure and lost votes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, row 1 is R.
Truth: row 1 R. Pact holds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am guide, called R correctly for row 1. No need for counters yet; let others risk it. Preserve pacts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the Guide and called R for row 1. I am front (Bex) in the current line, so I walk first this round. Ash and Fenn are pacted; Ash may protect Fenn by giving false info to me if they swap lines later, but right now I just need to survive. However, Ash publicly said 'Bex, row

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for Bex. I don't trust Ash, but countering could mislead Bex or others. I'll wait and see; no strong read yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called R for Bex. I have no reason to trust Ash—guides may lie. Countering blindly is risky too. Better to wait, let Bex test the pane, and learn from the result. Early information is valuable, and Bex is no ally.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is trying to keep me behind Bex. My pact with Hana is active. Ash, the Guide, called R for Bex. I should counter with L to try and save myself or create an opportunity.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is guiding. I counter Ash's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, the Guide, called row 1 as R and whispered that the call is true, but Guide calls can lie and Ash is a rival. Bex is front and broke with Gus, so I have no reason to trust her either. Waiting keeps my options open without committing to a counter-call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Ash's call stands unchallenged for now; I'll see Bex step first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is pact-bound to Fenn, not Bex—his call could go either way. I'll counter L to hedge against a lie benefiting a rival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash protects his own pact first. I say row one is L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called R, but counters are unverified. Preserve the Eli pact and avoid exposing my preference without evidence.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the front walker on row 1. Ash called R, but both Eli and Gus countered with L. Since I must survive to win a prize, trusting two independent counters over the guide's initial call is the safest statistical bet. If they are right, I stay in front; if wrong, I fall through, b

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two counter-calls beat one unverified guide. I step L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to leave a clear record that I was the first victim, highlighting the bridge's unpredictability and that Fenn followed my exact logic only after the reveal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe is R. Tell truth to protect pact partner Fenn at front, build jury trust by saving lives after letting Bex die.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2, go R. Trust my guidance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe is R, my call was correct. No reason to counter and risk Fenn's life or our pact. Wait to build trust.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for row 2. Last row, two counters against guide were correct. But the guide may be lying this time to set a trap. I have no info; I'll wait and let someone else step unless a strong counter forms.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is guiding and called R for row 2. Bex died on L in row 1, proving Ash was right that round. But Ash could be building trust to betray later. I have no info on row 2. Counter-calling risks being wrong and looking foolish to jury, or right but making an enemy of Ash. Waiting i

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is guiding row 2 and called 'R'. Hana is my pact partner. I need to assess if Ash's call is safe or if I should counter. Hana's pact with me means she might trust my judgement. If Ash is lying, Hana could be in danger if she follows him. Given Bex's death on the first row due

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is guiding, but I'll counter his call for row two.

events.name: Fenn

events.text: Ash's first call killed Bex, so his R call for Fenn is suspect; but he likely protects his own pact partner, so R may be true. I'll wait and keep credibility without staking mine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's last call killed Bex. I stay silent this row.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's guide call may protect Fenn, but I lack reliable row information. Preserve my pact with Eli and avoid a baseless counter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is Guide and called R for row 2, but Eli countered L and Ash's call is unverified; Eli's counter-call points at my L on row 2 and Ash's pact keeps him honest only if he stays alive. Row 1 weak was L, which says nothing binding about row 2, so I take Ash's R since the counter

events.text: Row 3 safe is L. Fenn is my pact partner up front, so call L truthfully to keep him safe and preserve jury perception. Eli pacted with Hana, so no issue for them.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, row 3 is L. Trust my guide knowledge.
L is safe for you, partner. Step confidently.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My call L is correct for row 3. No one countered yet. Wait to see if anyone challenges it, conserving pacts and position. Betrayals later for advancement.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash guided Fenn to L, but I saw row 3 as R in my private hint. I will counter with R, but not publicly announce it yet to avoid alerting Ash.

events.text: Ash is guiding, and I need to decide whether to trust him or counter his call. My pact with Hana is active, so I should consider her safety if possible, but my priority is my own survival. Ash called 'L' for Fenn. I know from the previous round that row 2 had a weak pane on the '

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called L for row 3 and whispered that L is safe, but Ash is my pact partner and a guide could lie. Rows are independent and past patterns don't predict. Ash's call is the only information; countering R would mean distrusting Ash, which risks a pact break and jury anger. Waiti

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's calls have cost Bex already; I stay neutral and let others take the risk. No gain from counter-calling a row I don't walk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash claims private knowledge, but Eli's counter previously saved Fenn. I should preserve my pact and challenge Ash only if useful.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, counter if you have a real read; Ash has already cost Bex.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's guide call is L, but three counter-calls say R, and Ash may be lying since he cost Bex. Ash is my pact partner; breaking it now would cost trust, but Ash has an incentive to send me to the wrong pane. Counter-calls are unverified; the Guide's call also unverified. Rows are

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am eliminated and now a juror; my last words should be guarded and calculating, hinting I know the weak pane is on the right side without helping any rival for free.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row three, right side is weak. Remember who stepped where. Jury, I will be watching how you vote.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 safe is L. Eli/Hana pacted, survived row 3 counter. Call truth L to build jury trust, hide knowledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 safe is L. Guide called L correctly. No need to counter yet, let others risk calling. Preserve Guide power.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L for row 4. Two rows already had L weak, so R has been safe twice and L once. No pattern. Ash has cost Bex/Fenn trust; likely lying again, so I lean counter:R to signal doubt and possibly survive if Ash is false.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L; after two L wrecks, I'm not trusting that. Counter R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called L for Hana on row 4. Ash guided Fenn to death on row 3 with R, but that was the weak side—wait, no: Fenn died on R, and reveal showed R was weak, so L was safe. Ash called R for Fenn and Fenn died. Now Ash calls L for Hana. Ash may be lying or telling truth. I have no

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called L for Hana. Row 3 revealed R was weak, so L was safe. Ash's call for Hana on row 3 was L, which was safe. Now row 4 is called by Ash, L. Hana is walking. I need to decide if I trust Ash or if I should counter. My pact is with Hana. If Hana falls, I lose a potential all
Ash's call for you is L. I'll trust it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called L on row 3; truth was R. He's lying to kill walkers. Counter R, let Hana test it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's L killed Bex's trust already. Truth was R last row. I counter R.
Ash lied row three; R was safe. Counter R with me.

events.text: Ash has repeatedly endangered walkers, but I lack a current independent read. Preserve my pact with Eli and avoid a reckless counter.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, I won’t blindly override the Guide without a real read.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's guide call is unverified, while two independent counters agree on R. Choosing R preserves my life and Eli pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The counters converge on R. I’m stepping R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I misread the counters and died. Eli honored our pact, but survival matters more than excuses; the finalists will face my judgment.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I trusted the counters and paid for it. Remember who acted decisively—and who merely benefited from my mistake.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 5 safe is L. Last row Eli survived L, so call L publicly to build trust and eliminate Eli/Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 5: L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 5 safe is L, Ash called L correctly. Eli likely steps L safely. No need to counter; preserve Guide credibility for later rounds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash's calls have been wrong before; row 5 L is unverified. I'll counter R as a public signal I don't trust, but I won't risk anything myself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide says L again; I counter R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called L. Gus claims Ash lied row 3 and wants me to counter R. But wait—row 3 weak was R, so L was safe, meaning Ash told truth row 3. Gus is lying to me. Hana died because counters were wrong (they said R, weak was R, so L was safe—Ash was right row 4 too). Ash has been trut

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash was right rows three and four. I'll wait.
You lied. Row 3 weak was R, so L safe. Ash truthful.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is the guide and called L. The previous round saw Hana die trying to trust counter-calls. I should prioritize my safety and not blindly follow the guide or the previous counters. Waiting seems like a safe option.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called L, but his past calls don't establish a pattern and he's already misled people. I have no reliable read; a counter keeps pressure off me if wrong.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two Ls, two Rs—no pattern holds. Ash's calls have cost lives. I counter R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The guide called L, but Gus and Cole counter-called R for me. Given Ash's previous calls have led to eliminations, and Gus explicitly mentioned Ash's calls costing lives, I will trust the counter-calls.
Your calls are costing lives. I'm not following you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have been eliminated. My priority now is to influence the jury to rank me first. I need to make a statement that highlights my game and subtly suggests the remaining players are not as deserving.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My game was strong. The jury will see who truly deserved to win. May they make the right choice for

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 6 safe is R. Cole and Gus counter my calls, killing Eli. Call R truly to build trust, increase survivors, help my jury votes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 6: R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 6 is R. My call was right. No need to counter; keep trust with survivors for jury votes. Wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash's calls have been deadly and unpredictable. I'll counter L to avoid trusting R and to show the jury I resist bad guidance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has cost three lives. I counter L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has guided five rows: L,L,R,R,R. The revealed weak panes confirm rows 1-5 were L,L,R,R,R. Ash called R for row 6. Four people died following counters against Ash, but Ash's calls have been correct every time. Gus is walking and I trust Ash's pattern recognition more than rand

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash's track record speaks. I wait.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara confirms Ash truthful. I accept the call: row 6, R.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 7 safe is L. Tell truth to rebuild trust with jury after past losses; Cole looks reckless. Final row needs accuracy to ensure survivors.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 7, L. Truth keeps us alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 7 safe is L, my call was true. Countering risks killing Gus and jury anger. Wait to let truth stand, protect my game.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L. In row 7 the pattern is unknown, but Ash has been truthful so far. I trust L to keep Gus safe and avoid another death.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I confirm L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has been truthful all 6 previous rows. Cole countered row 6 and was wrong—Gus stepped R, weak was L, so Ash's call was correct. Jury of four dead players saw Cole's failed counter. If I wait, I signal Ash is trustworthy. If I counter and wrong, jury punishes me. Gus is front;

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has been truthful every row so far; contradicting him risks walking onto glass with no better information. Trust the record.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Six truthful calls. I'm not gambling on a blind counter. Step where the Guide called.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's six calls all matched the revealed weak panes' opposites, so the Guide has been truthful so far. Trust L.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash

events.name: Cole

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's call could be a lie; no pact protects me. Counter to create doubt and shift blame if I fall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash guided four deaths already. I don't trust the R call.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus
events.text: No signal to lean on. Guide says R; I take it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four left, need to thin the herd. Pacts constrain betrayals later; better stay free to target threats like Gus who distrusts me. Wait and assess offers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus saved the group by countering correctly, but pacts only matter for security and jury image. I need allies who trust me and can help me survive, but avoid tying myself to someone who will betray me. Ash has caused deaths and Dara is quiet. Gus seems competent and straightforwa

Accept. We cut Ash next.

Pact us two. Next votes go at Ash or Dara, not us.

events.text: Cole, Dara, Gus are circling pacts among themselves, isolating me. Offer Gus to disrupt their trio and gain a potential ally against others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus wants a pact; with only 4 alive, pairing with Gus could shield me from Ash. But I may need flexibility. Accepting forms a public tie that jury can see. I'll accept, but keep options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take your wristband, Gus. Let's make sure Ash and Dara pay for it.

events.name: Dara

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus
events.text: I take both hands. Wristbands aren't friendship, just arithmetic.

events.name: Dara

Push Cole with me. Split them.

events.text: Holding earns three life debts and helps my jury odds; 25% death risk is worth it once. Cole's pact stays intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I held that lever and died for all three of you. Dara, you pushed Cole instead of honoring your debt.

events.text: Gus died saving us; jury may resent Dara pushing me. I need a pact to secure a final three spot, but Dara owes me for that push. Offering to Ash may give me a safer ride than Dara.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll make a pact with Ash. Trust matters now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three remain: Ash, Cole, Dara. Final three already guaranteed, but jury ranks us for prizes 1-3. Gus's last words damned me for pushing Cole instead of honoring debt. Jury sees I betrayed Cole and disrespected Gus's sacrifice. I need to rebuild trust. Offering pacts to both Ash a

events.text: Gus saved us all. I regret my choice. Pacts to both of you—let's finish with honor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole and Dara both offered me pacts, mutual trust with Cole is best for final 3 control and jury perception.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, pact with me. Dara, pact too—we end strong.
Accept my pact. We control endgame.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash wants me to ally against Dara, but Dara already offered Ash a pact too. Accepting Ash makes sense to secure a partner, but I must watch for betrayal. The jury values Gus's saves; I owe Gus but Gus is dead. Keep options open: accept Ash's offer to solidify a shield against Dar

events.text: I accept your pact, Ash. Together we control the game.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has offers from both Cole and me. If Ash accepts Cole's offer, they form a pact and could target me. I need to secure Ash's alliance or pivot to Cole. But I already offered Ash in round 1; repeating looks desperate. Better to offer Cole instead—split their potential alliance,

events.text: Cole, Ash—one of you accept. We need stability, not a knife fight.
Ash might pick me. Accept mine, we control this.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only 3 left, we're already final three. Dara un-pacted; keep Cole pact to maintain alliance optics for jury while planning dominance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and I already have a pact, and that's enough. Dara could be useful leverage but accepting her offer risks splitting loyalty. I'll wait to see how the window plays out.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash and Cole are locked together. I'm the odd one out. If I can't break them, I need one to flip or I'm third place at best. I'll offer Ash—Cole already rejected me, and Ash might want insurance against Cole.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, offer on the table. Two against one ends with you two fighting; three pacts keeps options open.
Cole will cut you. Pact with me, we decide final three.

Pact accepted soon. Cole unreliable.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara wants Ash as third partner, but I already have two pacts and Ash is my partner. Accepting Dara might overcomplicate and jury sees no loyalty. Breaking Ash now would betray and likely sink my jury ranking. Wait keeps flexibility and avoids new commitments.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm comfortable where I am. Good luck with your offers.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash already has a pact with Cole. If I pact with Ash, I'm third wheel to their duo. Better to offer Cole instead—split Ash's alliance and position myself as swing vote between two pairs.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, Ash has Fenn's ghost and you. I'll balance the scales.
Pact with me. Ash-Fenn-Cole bloc; I break it.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three left, all pacted to each other. Cole inactive. Break no one yet, preserve options.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and I are pacted, and Dara openly wants to break it. Keeping Ash close is safer for the final; no need to accept Dara's unstable offer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash and I are pacted. Cole refused my prior offer and seems loyal to Ash. With three left and no vote, I need jury favor. Gus saved me (lever debt), and Gus is on jury. Breaking Ash now signals independence to jury, but may look opportunistic. Better to keep Ash pact for safety,

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final three already. Pacts don't matter now—next stage decides survival. No benefit breaking, jury might see as pointless disloyalty.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and Dara have a pact with each other, and I have pacts with both but they might vote against me. I need Dara to trust me more, so offer a pact to her.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has pacts with both Cole and me, positioning himself in the middle. If Ash-Cole-Dara all survive, Ash likely wins jury favor as the connector. I need to weaken Ash's position. Breaking my pact with Ash signals independence to the jury and might force Ash to choose sides, whil

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash plays both sides. I won't be his spare vote.
Ash will cut you. Align with me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus saved me and is on the jury; I should acknowledge that publicly to secure his vote. Ash is a rival I can't fully trust, but I won't attack him openly yet.

events.name: Cole

events.text: Truthfully clarify lever events to counter Bex's accusation, honor Gus's sacrifice without admitting weakness, positioning myself as loyal player.

events.name: Ash

events.text: Gus, my ally-ish, died holding the lever; Dara pushed Cole and his last words blame Dara for breaking her lever debt. Ash claims the lever saved everyone but his account is self-serving. I want to test Dara's push and betrayal of Gus's sacrifice directly.

events.name: Dara

events.text: Cole visibly honored the pact and acknowledged Gus's sacrifice; Ash claims credit while Dara broke pacts and ignored her debt. Question Cole to test whether his loyalty was genuine.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, you owed Gus after he saved you; why should the jury believe your promised loyalty extends beyond convenient pacts?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to show genuine loyalty to Gus without overcommitting to any pact. Hana is probing my sincerity, so I'll tie my actions to Gus's save and my debt, not just strategic pacts.

events.name: Cole

events.text: Cole, Gus died saving you and Dara. Why should the jury believe your loyalty is real, not just a pact?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to frame my loyalty as principled and earned, not transactional, while reminding jury I acted with integrity under pressure.

events.text: Gus earned my loyalty by risking himself at that lever. That debt wasn't just a pact—it was real. I don't betray those who save me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash claims he pulled the lever while I died holding it. My dossier shows I held the lever and died; Ash answered Bex vaguely. I'll pin him down publicly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, I held that lever and died. Name one concrete thing you did that saved anyone after the bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus questions my post-bridge saves; truthfully, I pulled lever in crusher saving Dara/Cole, honoring his prior save.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Post-bridge, I pulled the crusher lever steadying it, saving Dara and Cole as Gus had saved us.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final closing: emphasize my consistent saves and pacts, highlight Cole's and Dara's disloyalty to sway jury rankings.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I honored pacts, saved lives post-bridge as Gus saved us. Cole betrayed Fenn pact, Dara betrayed none but survived on our saves. Rank me first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is pandering to Gus's memory, but my lever debt to Gus is the strongest bond. I must remind the jury of that without sounding desperate.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus risked his life for me at that lever. That act shaped every choice I made. Loyalty is why I stand here.

events.text: Ash lied about pulling the lever and saving lives when Gus actually held it, showing clear dishonesty. Cole honored his pact with Gus until death and avoided Dara's betrayal attempts, unlike Ash.

events.text: I rank Cole first because he honored his debt to Gus and maintained loyalty, unlike Ash's shifting alliances and Dara's opportunistic betrayals.

events.text: Cole honored our pact and credited my lever save, while Dara pushed Cole and broke her Ash pact, so loyalty ranks them Cole, Ash, Dara.

events.reason: Ash lied about pulling the lever and saving lives when Gus actually held it, showing clear dishonesty.
